source_documents.document: China Life Insurance Co. Ltd. 2005 Form 20-F
source_documents.finding: NYSE ADSs each represented H shares; the filing identifies H shares as a class of the issuer's capital/common stock.

source_documents.document: China Life Insurance Co. Ltd. 2007 Form 20-F
source_documents.finding: The issuer records the December 2006 ADS ratio change from 40 H shares per ADS to 15 H shares per ADS, preserving the same H-share underlying class.

cases.factual_findings: CUSIP 16939P106 is the China Life ADS program representing H shares. H shares are ordinary/common equity; an ADS wrapper does not change that class under the contract.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: Single canonical CUSIP. The 2006 depositary ratio change altered shares-per-ADS, not the legal class of the deposited H shares.
cases.contradiction_search: Issuer filings distinguish H shares/ADSs from other capital descriptions and provide no evidence that CUSIP 16939P106 represented preferred stock, partnership/trust units, warrants, rights, or another non-common class during the canonical interval.

source_documents.document: Citi Mechel depositary-program profile for CUSIP 583840103
source_documents.finding: The predecessor ADR program was active from 2004; a 2016 reverse ADS split changed CUSIP 583840103 to 583840608.
The filing explicitly identifies Mechel common shares and American Depositary Shares, each ADS representing common shares; Mechel's preferred ADS is a distinct security.

cases.factual_findings: MTL was the sponsored ADS on Mechel common shares. The preferred ADS program was a distinct security/ticker and is not this canonical episode.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: CUSIP 583840103 identifies the common-share ADS program during the canonical interval. CUSIP 583840608 is its later successor after a reverse ADS split/ratio change; the transition preserves the common-share underlying class and does not indicate a type change.
cases.contradiction_search: Primary records explicitly distinguish the common-share ADS from Mechel's preferred-share ADS. No evidence ties either assigned CUSIP to the preferred program.

source_documents.finding: CUSIP 25382P109 is explicitly Common Stock.
A reverse split of common stock produced successor CUSIP 25382T200.
A 1-for-20 reverse split of common stock produced CUSIP 25382T309.
A subsequent 1-for-100 reverse split of common stock produced CUSIP 25382T408.
Digital Ally changed its corporate name/ticker to Kustom Entertainment/KUST and completed a 1-for-3 reverse split of common stock, yielding CUSIP 25382T507.
CUSIP 25382T606 is explicitly Common Stock.

cases.factual_findings: The assigned CUSIPs form a succession of Digital Ally/Kustom Entertainment common-stock identifiers associated with reverse splits and the 2026 issuer name/ticker transition. SEC-filed ownership records also identify intermediate assigned identifiers as common stock/common equity.
cases.identity_transition_analysis: The many CUSIP changes are corporate-action identity changes in one common-stock lineage. Reverse splits change share count/CUSIP; the Digital Ally-to-Kustom Entertainment name/ticker change preserves the equity class. No evidence establishes a legal type change anywhere in the canonical interval.
cases.contradiction_search: Searched SEC and Nasdaq records around the assigned CUSIPs and split/name-change events. Records consistently call the security common stock; no assigned identifier was found to be preferred, a unit, warrant, right, trust interest, partnership interest, or bundled hybrid.
